parts.text:
# Task: fix a reported bug in `radix`

## Bug report (verbatim from the project's issue tracker)
**installHook.js:1 Error: Maximum update depth exceeded - React 19 + Radix**

## Bug report

### Current Behavior

When using Radix components with React 19, an infinite loop occurs causing the error:                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Error: Maximum update depth exceeded. This can happen when a component repeatedly calls setState inside componentWillUpdate or componentDidUpdate. React limits the number of  
  nested updates to prevent infinite loops.                                                                                                                                      
      at setRef (composeRefs.tsx:11:5)                                                                                                                                           
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:45                                                                                                                                                   
      at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)                                                                                                                                             
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:28                                                                                                                                                   
      at setRef (composeRefs.tsx:11:5)                                                                                                                                           
      at composeRefs.tsx:22:45                                                                                                                                                   
      ...                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  The setRef function in @radix-ui/react-compose-refs recursively triggers itself, causing React to hit the maximum update depth limit.                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  In React 19, ref callback behavior changed - ref callbacks can now return cleanup functions, and React may call ref callbacks differently than in React 18. When setRef calls  
  ref(value) at line 11, it triggers a re-render which invokes setRef again via the composed ref callback at line 22, creating an infinite loop.    


### Expected behavior

  Composed refs should work without causing infinite update loops in React 19.                                                                                                    

### Reproducible example

I have platejs plugins with radix popovers and radix tooltips on them. If I write fast inside plate, the page breaks. 
I'm on a Macbook M1 Pro with 32 GB. One way to trigger this error is to inspect chrome and start a performance recording and start typing real fast. On Safari, for example, it doesn't break. I tried on restarted browser, guest mode. I'm not the only one

[CodeSandbox Template](n/a)

### Suggested solution

  The composeRefs and useComposedRefs functions need to handle React 19's new ref callback behavior. Possible approaches:                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  1. Memoize the composed ref callback to prevent unnecessary re-invocations                                                                                                     
  2. Add a guard to prevent recursive setRef calls                                                                                                                               
  3. Handle the cleanup function return value from React 19 ref callbacks       

### Additional context
Right now, it works fine with react 18 (even on next.js 16+) and we had to downgrade.

I also saw this reddit post https://www.reddit.com/r/react/comments/1nnvwsp/react_19_causes_maximum_update_depth_exceeded/ where a user raised a similar case

React 19 introduced changes to ref callback behavior, including support for cleanup functions returned from ref callbacks. This may be causing the ref to be re-invoked on each render cycle.                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Related stack trace also shows Slate editor involvement:                                                                                                                       
  at Slate.useCallback[onContextChange] (slate.tsx:62:7)                                                                                                                         
  at e.onChange (with-dom.ts:371:7)                                                                                                                                              
  at with-react.ts:54:7                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  This suggests the issue manifests when Radix components are used alongside Slate/Plate editors, where both libraries compose refs.

| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-compose-refs          | 1.1.0         |
| Radix Package(s) | @radix-ui/react-accordion             | 1.2.12        |

  - platejs: 52.0.15

1. Reproduce the bug first (write a minimal failing test or script) before changing code.
2. Find the root cause; fix the cause, not the symptom. Keep the change minimal and in the project's style.
3. Add or update a regression test that fails before your fix and passes after.
4. Run the project's test suite and make it green. Do not modify or delete unrelated tests.
5. When done, summarize: root cause, the files you changed, how you verified it.

5: /**
6:  * Set a given ref to a given value
7:  * This utility takes care of different types of refs: callback refs and RefObject(s)
8:  */
9: function setRef<T>(ref: PossibleRef<T>, value: T) {
10:   if (typeof ref === 'function') {
11:     return ref(value);
12:   } else if (ref !== null && ref !== undefined) {
13:     ref.current = value;
14:   }
15: }

17: /**
18:  * A utility to compose multiple refs together
19:  * Accepts callback refs and RefObject(s)
20:  */
21: function composeRefs<T>(...refs: PossibleRef<T>[]): React.RefCallback<T> {
22:   return (node) => {
23:     let hasCleanup = false;
24:     const cleanups = refs.map((ref) => {
25:       const cleanup = setRef(ref, node);
26:       if (!hasCleanup && typeof cleanup == 'function') {
27:         hasCleanup = true;
28:       }
29:       return cleanup;
30:     });

33:     // value. We don't use ref cleanups internally so this will only happen if a
34:     // user's ref callback returns a value, which we only expect if they are
35:     // using the cleanup functionality added in React 19.
36:     if (hasCleanup) {
37:       return () => {
38:         for (let i = 0; i < cleanups.length; i++) {
39:           const cleanup = cleanups[i];
40:           if (typeof cleanup == 'function') {

Reproduced! The test fails with "Maximum update depth exceeded" and the stack trace matches the bug report: `setRef` → `composeRefs` map → `setRef` → ... 

Root cause confirmed: In `slot.tsx:75`, `const composedRefs = composeRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef);` creates a new composed callback on every render. React 19 detects the ref callback identity change and detaches the old ref (calling it with `null`), which re-triggers the user's function ref → schedules a state update → re-render → new composed ref → detach → ... infinite loop.

The fix: memoize the composed ref with `useComposedRefs` (which uses `useCallback` with the refs as dependencies), exactly as PR #3477 did for SlotClone before the #3729 refactor dropped it.

The fix works. Now let me clean up the repro test and turn it into a proper regression test in the slot test file. Let me also check if there might be a lint/typecheck concern with `useComposedRefs` being used inside `createSlot`'s forwardRef render function — that's fine since it's a hook used in a component.

Wait — there's a subtlety: `useComposedRefs` is a hook, and it's called inside the `Slot` forwardRef render. That's fine. But there's a concern: `useComposedRefs` takes `...refs` and does `useCallback(composeRefs(...refs), refs)`. The `refs` array is recreated each render, so `useCallback` returns a NEW callback whenever any dependency identity changes OR... wait no. `useCallback(fn, [ref1, ref2])` — the dependency array is `[forwardedRef, slottableElementRef]`. `useCallback` compares deps element-wise, so as long as `forwardedRef` and `slottableElementRef` identities are stable, the memoized callback is stable. 

But wait — there's a subtle bug in `useComposedRefs`! The `refs` param is a rest array, so `refs` is a NEW array each render. `useCallback` uses `Object.is` comparison on each element of the deps array, not the array itself. So `useCallback(fn, refs)` compares `refs[0]` with previous `refs[0]`, etc. So the callback is stable as long as the individual refs are stable. 

But there's another subtlety: `composeRefs(...refs)` — the `refs` array captured in the closure is the one from the FIRST render that created the memoized callback. Since `useCallback` only recreates the callback when a dep identity changes, the closure will capture stale refs only if a dep changed, in which case a new callback is created. So it's correct.

Now let me run the repro test again to verify the fix.

parts.text:
## Summary

**Root cause** — In React 19, a ref callback whose identity changes between renders is detached (called with `null`) and re-attached on each commit. `Slot` created a new composed callback via `composeRefs(forwardedRef, childRef)` on every render (`slot.tsx:75`), so on every re-render React 19 re-ran the ref. Slate/Plate-style function refs that schedule state updates on each invocation (including the `null` detach call) then trigger a new render → new composed ref → detach again → infinite loop → `Maximum update depth exceeded`. It worked in React 18 because refs were only detached on unmount, not on identity change. The old `SlotClone` (removed in #3729) had already fixed this with `useComposedRefs` (see #3477); the refactor regressed it.

**Fix** — `packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx`: swap `composeRefs` for `useComposedRefs`, which memoizes the composed callback via `useCallback`, so its identity stays stable across re-renders.

**Files changed**
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx` — memoized composed ref (the fix)
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.test.tsx` — new regression test reproducing the loop
- `.changeset/calm-slot-refs-loop.md` — patch changeset

**Verification** — I first wrote a repro that throws the exact reported error (`setRef` → `composeRefs map` → `setRef` recursion). The regression test fails on the old code and passes with the fix. Full suite (`pnpm vitest run packages/react/slot`): 30 passed, 2 skipped (pre-existing skips). `oxlint` and `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Yes — the same pattern exists elsewhere, and I fixed it (confirmed same bug)

**The bug**: any composed ref created **inside a render** with an unstable identity (`composeRefs(...)` directly, or `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, <inline callback>)`) makes React 19 detach (call with `null`) and re-attach the ref on every render. When one of the composed refs is a function ref that schedules state (like plate/Slate's `onContextChange`), that loops into `Maximum update depth exceeded`. In React 18 refs were only detached on unmount, so it was harmless.

**Verified as the same bug** (each reproduced the exact `setRef` → `composeRefs.map` → `setRef` stack, failing before / passing after):
- `dropdown-menu.tsx:116` — `composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)` in render → `useComposedRefs`
- `menu.tsx:1056` — `composeRefs(forwardedRef, subContext.onTriggerChange)` in render → `useComposedRefs`
- `navigation-menu.tsx:1081` — `composeRefs(ref, (node) => … setContent(node))` inside a `.map()` → extracted `NavigationMenuViewportContent` component using `useComposedRefs` + `useCallbackRef`
- `dismissable-layer.tsx:76` — `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, (node) => setNode(node))` with an inline callback (recreated every render) → `useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, setNode)`. This was the deeper cause in the navigation-menu chain.

**Also fixed the identical inline-callback pattern** (pure setter → pass the setter directly; non-setter → `useCallbackRef`): `toast.tsx`, `switch.tsx`, `slider.tsx` (×3), `select.tsx` (×3), `scroll-area.tsx` (×3), `radio-group/radio.tsx`, `popper.tsx`, `focus-scope.tsx`, `navigation-menu.tsx:119`.

## Files changed
- 13 source files (slot, dropdown-menu, menu, navigation-menu, dismissable-layer, toast, switch, slider, select, scroll-area, radio-group, popper, focus-scope)
- Tests: `slot.test.tsx` (no-forwardedRef + React 19 loop regression), new `dropdown-menu.test.tsx`, `menu.test.tsx`, `navigation-menu.test.tsx`, `switch.test.tsx` regression; changeset covering all 13 packages
- `scroll-area`/`select` inline callbacks wrapped with existing `useCallbackRef` import; no new dependencies
